fluff.overview:
The Dasher II is a forty-ton medium BattleMech introduced in 3077 by Clan Diamond Shark as a heavier, non-OmniMech successor to the venerable Fire Moth. Designed explicitly for the Inner Sphere export market, the Dasher II was produced at Manufacturing Plant DSF-IT1 on Itabaiana and aboard the DSS Poseidon, a Potemkin-class WarShip serving as a mobile production facility. The design retained the original Dasher's emphasis on extreme speed while doubling its mass, ostensibly providing a sturdier platform for raiding and reconnaissance operations.

The Sharks' true motivation for producing the Dasher II appears to have been primarily commercial and technological. Sold at or below cost to Inner Sphere states and fellow Clans alike, the design served as both a revenue generator and a stepping stone toward more advanced propulsion technologies with far broader implications for the Diamond Shark product line.
fluff.capabilities:
The Dasher II's defining characteristic is its massive Type 79 400-rated extralight engine, which consumes nearly two-thirds of the 'Mech's available tonnage to achieve a cruising speed of 108 kilometers per hour and a top speed of 162. This engine dominance leaves precious little weight for weapons and protection. Three tons of Compound 6F ferro-fibrous armor provide marginally better protection than the Fire Moth, but the Dasher II remains woefully underarmored for a medium 'Mech, carrying less protection than many light designs.

Armament consists of six Mustang 4.5 extended-range micro lasers, weapons with an effective engagement range of only 120 meters. While capable of inflicting serious damage in massed close-range fire, this loadout effectively negates any technological advantage Clan weaponry typically provides over Inner Sphere opponents. The Dasher II must close to knife-fighting range to be effective, exposing its thin armor to sustained long-range fire during the approach.

The design also suffers from poor acceleration characteristics, requiring considerable time to reach its impressive top speed. This sluggish throttle response compounds the vulnerability created by its short-ranged armament, as pilots cannot rely on rapid bursts of speed to evade incoming fire during the critical approach phase of an engagement.
fluff.history:
The Dasher II emerged from Clan Diamond Shark's expanding Inner Sphere commercial operations during the closing years of the Jihad. Production began in 3077 at two facilities tied to the Shark enclave on Itabaiana: the ground-based Manufacturing Plant DSF-IT1 and Auxiliary Production Site #4 aboard the DSS Poseidon, a Potemkin-class WarShip. Republic of the Sphere intelligence analysts long puzzled over the Diamond Sharks' decision to produce what appeared to be an inferior design at a facility that was not only non-OmniMech capable but also served as their primary research and development center.

The Sharks offered the Dasher II to both Inner Sphere and Clan buyers almost immediately upon its introduction. Stone's Coalition procured a number of units prior to its invasion of the Word of Blake Protectorate in 3077, and the design entered service with the Republic Armed Forces following the Coalition's victory. Despite the availability of more cost-effective alternatives, limited quantities found their way into the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns, Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces, and Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery. Among the Clans, Clan Ghost Bear, Clan Nova Cat, and Clan Snow Raven were noted operators of the design.

The mystery of the Dasher II's existence became clearer with the appearance of the Dasher II 2 in 3084. The Sharks' merchant caste had sold the original at a loss specifically to accelerate funding and development of the Model 53b XXL engine, an experimental propulsion system costing nearly three times as much as the base Dasher II. This engine technology proved to have far-reaching implications for the Diamond Shark product line, with XL versions of the Type 79 engine already appearing in multiple Phoenix Hawk IIC variants and the Warhammer IIC 8.

By the Dark Age era, continued production at both Itabaiana facilities ensured a steady supply of Dasher IIs and their improved variants. The introduction of the radically redesigned Dasher II 3 and Dasher II 4 in 3136 demonstrated that the chassis had evolved well beyond its origins as a simple speed platform, incorporating mixed-technology solutions including Inner Sphere close-combat equipment and advanced armor systems. Clan Sea Fox, successor to the Diamond Sharks, maintained production through the ilClan era, continuing the design's role as an accessible and widely exported combat platform.
fluff.deployment: Also entering service in 3136, the Dasher II 4 is an advanced mixed-technology brawler built around close-combat engagement. Triple Strength Myomer and a chain whip provide devastating melee capability, while an XXL engine and XL gyro free tonnage for an unusually diverse weapons suite: paired LRM-5 launchers for long-range harassment, an ER large laser and ER medium laser for sustained direct fire, and an ER small laser paired with a micro pulse laser for point-blank engagements. Eight improved jump jets grant an impressive 240-meter jump radius, and hardened armor provides exceptional physical protection suited to the variant's intended role. With a base speed of 100 kilometers per hour increasing to 110 when Triple Strength Myomer activates, the Dasher II 4 sacrifices raw speed for a level of tactical versatility unimaginable in the original design.
